title: Reliability Theater: Ops Roadmap (90d)
body:
Elevator pitch:
This doc frames a 90-day, cross-functional plan to operationalize the reliability program using an "operational theater" metaphor. The goal is to create repeatable rituals, lightweight playbooks, and a prioritized SLO portfolio that feature teams can adopt without heavy process overhead.

Why "Reliability Theater"?
- Theater = defined stages (canary, ramp, steady state) + roles (director = product owner, stage manager = SRE, actors = feature teams).
- Helps teams reason about transitions: deploy -> observe -> roll-forward/rollback -> learn.
- Emphasizes rehearsals (chaos-lite, tabletop runbooks) before public performance (production rollout).

Scope (what's in / out):
- In: service-level objectives for public-facing HTTP APIs, background jobs that impact customer SLAs, cross-service latency dependencies, error budget instrumentation, oncall playbooks for SLO breaches.
- Out: infra-only capacity planning (separate), model training pipelines (handled by applied-ml), long-tail internal tools with no customer-facing impact.

Primary outcomes (90d):
1) Baseline SLO portfolio for top 12 services (by customer impact & traffic) with owner sign-off.
2) 3 reproducible canary rehearsals and one formal tabletop escalation exercise.
3) SLO observability kit: standard dashboards, burn-rate alert templates, and one-click incident stub.
4) Lightweight rollout playbook integrated in release process (PR checklist + canary gating).
5) Evidence of error budget-driven behavior in at least two feature teams (blocked releases or mitigations triggered).

Principles / constraints:
- Keep it pragmatic: default SLO templates, not bespoke for every microservice.
- Minimize process: adopt a "guardrail not gate" approach for most teams.
- Automate early: instrument once, reuse many times (dashboards, alerts as code).
- Safety first: all rollouts have a fallback corridor (automated downgrade or fallback region).
- Measurable: each deliverable has at least one numeric KPI.

Success metrics (KPIs):
- SLO coverage: percentage of top-12 services with a defined SLO and owner (target: 100%).
- Time to detect: median time from user-visible deviation to alert (target: <= 90s for critical SLOs).
- Error budget actions: number of releases automatically gated or rolled back when burn rate > 5x (target: 2+ in 90d).
- Mean time to repair (MTTR) for SLO incidents (target: reduce by 30% vs baseline).

90-day roadmap (high level weeks):
- Week 0-2: Kickoff + prioritization workshop (Platform + SRE + product + applied-ml + obs). Create SLO candidate list for top services.
- Week 3-5: Draft SLOs + measurement owners assigned. Build dashboards and alert templates (obs infra).
- Week 6-8: Canary rehearsals with two feature teams; tabletop escalation run with exec observers. Iterate on runbooks.
- Week 9-11: Integrate SLO checks into release flow (PR gating, CI smoke tests + canary gating).
- Week 12: Review, retro, and deployable playbook publish + adoption commitments. Executive one-pager for leadership.

Detailed milestones (deliverables):
- SLO portfolio CSV (owner, target, window, signal source, query id).
- Dashboard kit: 1 page template per SLO type (availability, latency, saturation).
- Alert templates: burn-rate alert (4 levels), SLO down alert (pager + async).
- Rollout playbook: 1-page flowchart + checklist for canary limits + automated rollback triggers.
- Rehearsal artifacts: tabletop notes, decision logs, after-action items.

Roles & responsibilities (practical names):
- Director (Maya Chen): program owner, collates decisions, exec updates.
- Stage Manager (SRE lead, Jonah Ruiz): builds observability kit, runs rehearsals.
- Feature Owners (product + eng reps): sign SLOs, participate in canaries.
- Observability SME (Evelyn Park): dashboards, query templates, alert tuning.
- Release Engineering (Samir Patel): integrate canary gating into CI/CD.
- Customer Success liaison (Laura Green): validate SLO choices against customer pain.

RACI (short form):
- Define SLO targets: R = Feature Owner, A = Director, C = SRE, I = CS/Product.
- Implement dashboards: R = Observability SME, A = Stage Manager, C = Feature Owner, I = Director.
- Run tabletop: R = Stage Manager, A = Director, C = All stakeholders, I = Exec observers.

Cross-functional rituals (cadence):
- Weekly "SLO theater" sync (30m): rapid unblock, feature owners report progress.
- Bi-weekly rehearsal (60m): live canary / rollback dry-run.
- Ad-hoc war-room (triggered): if burn rate > 10x for 15m.
- Monthly leadership digest: 1-pager on coverage, incidents, and adoption.

Experiment matrix (priority lanes):
- Lane A (urgent high impact): top 4 services by revenue/customer priority -> full SLO + automated gating.
- Lane B (medium): next 8 services -> SLO + dashboards + manual gating.
- Lane C (low): long tail -> guidance + optional instrumentation.

Safety & fallback patterns (examples):
- Circuit-breaker downgrade: if p99 latency crosses X, route to lower-capacity model variant.
- Capacity corridor: burst to dedicated pool (Dedicated capacity) with auto-fall back to hosted variants.
- Incremental rollout: 1% -> 10% -> 50% steps with automated checkpoints for error budget.

Risks and mitigations (notes):
- Risk: Measurement drift / noisy signals -> Mitigation: define a 7d smoothing window for alerting; run data-quality jobs.
- Risk: Teams feel process overhead -> Mitigation: provide templates, pairing sessions, and platform-backed gates (easy to opt-in).
- Risk: False positives during global incidents -> Mitigation: global-incident flag to temporarily mute burn-rate alerts and rely on human bridge.

Open questions / discussion items (for kickoff):
- What SLI backfills are required for services without historical telemetry? (obs estimate: 2-3 weeks per service)
- Agreement on default SLO tiers (Gold / Silver / Bronze) and mapping to business metrics.
- Which releases are considered high-risk enough to require automated gating?

Communication plan:
- Immediate: create a short Confluence intro + links to dashboard kit.
- Weekly: SLO theater sync notes + action items in shared board (JIRA-INF-937).
- Exec: monthly one-pager and a demo at the platform review meeting.

Adoption nudges (how we'll get teams onboard):
- "Starter kit" templates and a 2-hour office hours offering with Observability SME.
- Quick wins: instrument a caching tier and show cost/latency improvements in 2 weeks.
- Recognition: badge in internal directory for "SLO Compliant" services.

Budget / resourcing snapshot:
- SRE allocation: 0.5 FTE Jonah (lead) + ad-hoc rotation 0.2 FTE per participating SRE.
- Observability: 0.3 FTE Evelyn for the 90d window.
- Release engineering: 0.2 FTE Samir for CI changes.
- Estimate: 4-6 engineering sprints of focused work across teams.

Post-90d follow-up (sustainability):
- Transition to "SLO steward" rotation across Platform and SRE.
- Quarterly SLO health review (include customer success and product).
- Automate runbook generation from incident playbook after 1st 3 incidents.

Appendix (practical templates and examples included in Confluence):
- Example availability SLO: 99.95% over 30d window for /v1/generate (primary endpoint).
- Example latency SLO: p95 < 250ms over 7d rolling window for small payloads.
- Burn-rate alert thresholds: 3x (inform), 5x (action), 10x (pager).

Notes to self / to-do list at next sync:
- [ ] Finalize top-12 service list with Product by 2026-01-22.
- [ ] Create dashboard kit repo and add query IDs by 2026-02-05.
- [ ] Schedule two rehearsal windows w/ feature teams (target Wk6 & Wk8).
- [ ] Draft exec one-pager and leadership invite for demo week (Wk12).

Unpolished fragments / brainstorming (internal):
- Could we route low-priority traffic to quantized model variants automatically for cheaper capacity in emergencies? (requires integration w/ Dedicated routing policy).
- Short experiment: enable a global muted alarm flag for 10m windows to reduce alert fatigue during flapping deployments.

Contact / owners:
- Program owner: Maya Chen (maya@redwood.com)
- SRE lead: Jonah Ruiz (jonah@redwood.com)
- Observability: Evelyn Park (evelyn@redwood.com)

End of doc.
